caption:
5 handbags everyone is wearing in Paris right now 🇫🇷
If you want to understand real Parisian handbag style, it is not only about the most obvious designer bags. In Paris, the bags French women actually wear are often practical, understated, and easy to style every day.
Mini Marly by Ateliers Auguste
A chic everyday French bag — structured, minimal, and very Parisian without feeling too obvious.
Céline Bucket Bag
The perfect understated designer bag. Elegant, discreet, and easy to wear with jeans, tailoring, or a simple summer dress.
Le City by Balenciaga
The cool-girl Paris bag. A little messy, effortless, nostalgic, and perfect if you like a more relaxed French style.
Longchamp Le Pliage
The real-life French woman bag. Practical, lightweight, and still one of the most common bags you will see in Paris.
Saint Louis by Goyard
The old-money Parisian tote. Spacious, classic, and instantly recognizable, but still more discreet than many logo bags.
Parisian handbag style is all about balance: practical but elegant, designer but not too flashy, polished but never too perfect.

When people imagine packing for ten days in Europe, they often picture ten outfits.

In reality, the goal is much simpler: build a small wardrobe where everything works together.

Instead of thinking in outfits, I plan in layers and combinations. A few well-chosen pieces can create far more than ten looks once you start mixing them thoughtfully.

When I’m packing for a trip like this, I walk through a simple framework:
• Start with a base palette. Choose two or three core colors so everything mixes easily.�• Add layers that cooperate. A knit, a blazer, and a coat should all work together comfortably.�• Choose bottoms that repeat well. Trousers, denim, or a skirt that can anchor multiple outfits.�• Pack shoes that support the itinerary. One true walking shoe, one polished option, and one that slightly elevates the wardrobe.�• Make sure every piece works at least three ways.

Once those pieces are in place, the combinations come naturally. Getting dressed becomes easy because everything already belongs together.

This is exactly the approach I used to create my Spring in Europe: The Style + Packing Guide.
